evidence: src/application/list-stock-levels-use-case.ts: ListStockLevelsUseCase.validateExecute(request: PlaceOrderRequest) imports PlaceOrderRequest from ./dtos and throws InvalidRequestError("customerId is required"). This is order-placement validation inside a stock-listing use case.

src/application/place-order-use-case.ts: PlaceOrderUseCase.execute already runs `if (!request.customerId) throw new InvalidRequestError("customerId is required")`, so the same rule is written in two places.
src/application/dtos.ts: PlaceOrderRequest is the order-placement input DTO. Its only intended user is PlaceOrderUseCase, but ListStockLevelsUseCase also uses it.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of the module holds together. Each use case lives in its own file, loads aggregates through the domain repositories and maps results with the shared toOrderDto/toStockLevelDto helpers in dtos.ts. The exception is ListStockLevelsUseCase in list-stock-levels-use-case.ts. Besides its read-only stock listing, it has a validateExecute(request: PlaceOrderRequest) method. That method validates order placement, which belongs to a different use case. It also repeats the rule "customerId is required" (throw new InvalidRequestError("customerId is required")), which PlaceOrderUseCase.execute already enforces in place-order-use-case.ts. So one rule lives in two places, and the stock-listing use case is mixed with an order-placement concern. Smaller duplications, such as the find-or-throw NotFoundError check repeated in the cancel, get and transition use cases, are ordinary use-case boilerplate and are not the main finding.

violations.message: ListStockLevelsUseCase.validateExecute(request: PlaceOrderRequest) adds order-placement validation to the stock-listing use case. It also repeats the 'customerId is required' rule that PlaceOrderUseCase.execute already enforces, so the rule is no longer kept in one place.
PlaceOrderUseCase.execute has its own copy of the 'customerId is required' check (InvalidRequestError), and ListStockLevelsUseCase.validateExecute repeats it. This rule should live in one place.
